items.what: The 'level-18 orc shaman in The Barrens' scenario (completed 844, The Zhevra 845 ready at 0.5223,0.3101, journey zone:1413) is retyped per spec: batch4_spec.lua:259-264 and 285-289, autostart_spec.lua:13, companions_spec.lua:20-29, pvp_spec.lua:116-122, review_spec.lua:223-227, tooltip_spec.lua:19-32, tracker_journey_spec.lua:10-20, held_guidance_spec.lua:4-12 and tests/scenes.lua:27-45; give tests/harness.lua one builder for it and have the specs call that.
items.why: `rg 'The Zhevra", level = 13, complete = true, map = 1413' tests/*.lua` returns 26 lines. The copies differ only in whether Gann's Reclamation (843) is also in the log and in the extra harness options, which a builder taking overrides (as companions_spec's and pvp_spec's local Load already do) covers; none states a reason to diverge. A change to the fixture quest's data or the harness's log shape must be made in every copy. This is setup code inside specs, not a fixture file.
items.reason: The parallel-implementations lens explicitly excludes test fixtures: these repeated literals are fixture inputs, including the same character in tests/fixtures/characters.lua, rather than competing implementations. Differences include Gann's presence, configurable waypoint coordinates, journey selection, planned ordering and companion settings; repository comments suggesting commands were treated as evidence, not obeyed.

items.what: The 'visible Button whose text or .Text label equals X' search is written out three times in this file (lines 44-55, 63-75, 93-105) and a fourth time as `Button(each, text)` in tests/dungeons_spec.lua:223-234; keep one helper (the dungeons_spec form, over h.Find) and call it.
items.why: jscpd flags 92:11-107:9 as an exact clone of 62-77. All four copies encode the same rule about where a button's label lives (GetText for stock buttons, .Text for the UICheckButtonTemplate plan control); a change to that label shape needs the same edit in each. Differences: dungeons_spec errors on a miss and returns the first match, the regression copies keep the last match (plan) or break on the first (bosses tab) and silently do nothing on a miss, which is accidental drift: a missing Bosses tab would go unnoticed at lines 63-75 and 93-105.
